   Successor Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency Agenda Report
  August 6, 2024

TO:  Honorable Agency Members

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, Executive Director

BY:  Alexander Hamilton, Interim Director of Community Development
  Jana Stuard, Finance Officer
  Arnold M. Alvarez-Glasman, City Attorney
  Austin A. Ching, Deputy City Attorney

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. SA 24-02 - AUTHORIZING THE TRANSFER OF A
  PROPERTY (12710 NORWALK BOULEVARD) PURSUANT TO THE LONG-
  RANGE PROPERTY MANAGEMENT PLAN

Background:

On April 9, 2014, the State of California Department of Finance (“DOF”) notified the Successor
Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency (“Successor Agency”) that the Successor
Agency’s Long-Range Property Management Plan (“LRPMP”) was approved. Within the
LRPMP, the Successor Agency stated its intent to transfer the property located at 12710 Norwalk
Boulevard, Accessor Parcel Number (APN) 8047-006-922 (“Property”), to the County of Los
Angeles (“County”) for use as a parking structure for judges from the adjacent County
courthouse.

The parcel for the Judges’ parking structure was created through the implementation of an
Option Agreement for Transfer of Real Property by and between the Norwalk Redevelopment
Agency and the County of Los Angeles dated February 5, 2002, and subsequently amended. A
new Option Agreement was entered into on May 19, 2009, and has also been subsequently
amended. The Successor Agency constructed a 25-space enclosed, secured parking structure
for the judges of the Superior Court. The structure has been completed and is currently used
by judges for parking.

Title to the City-owned lot on which the judges’ parking lot is built was originally held by the
Norwalk Redevelopment Agency (“RDA”). When the RDA was dissolved pursuant to AB 1x26
(the “Dissolution Act”) and the California Supreme Court decision in California Redevelopment
 Successor Agency to the Norwalk Redevelopment Agency  August 6, 2024
12710 Norwalk Blvd Property Transfer to the City of Norwalk  Page No. 2

Association, et al. v. Ana Matosantos, et al. 53 Cal.4th 231 (2011), the Property was transferred
to the Successor Agency.

The Dissolution Act (Health and Safety Code §34181(a)) allows for the Oversight Board of the
Successor Agency to direct the Successor Agency to transfer the ownership of assets that were
constructed and used for a governmental purpose pursuant to existing agreements. In 2018,
the Oversight Boards of all Successor Agencies in the County of Los Angeles were consolidated
into five districts, with the City of Norwalk falling under the jurisdiction of the Fourth District
Oversight Board (“Oversight Board”).

The definition of “governmental purpose” included parking facilities that do not generate
revenues in excess of reasonable maintenance costs of the properties. The transfer of the
Property must be approved by the Oversight Board, pursuant to a resolution and a public
meeting with ten (10) days advanced notice. As the Property is to be exchanged with another
adjacent parcel for the City’s parking purposes, the exchange needs to occur between the City
and County, rather than the Successor Agency. Therefore, prior to any exchange with the
County, the Successor Agency needs to transfer the Property to the City, and the City needs to
accept via the attached resolutions.

The transfer of the Property is also exempt from the Surplus Land Act (AB 1486) under California
Government Code §54221(f)(1)(C) and §54221(f)(1)(D) in that the Property is being transferred
to another local agency’s use for the purpose of eventually exchanging the parcel for another
property necessary for the agency’s use; and

The transfer is also exempt from the requirements of the California Environmental Quality Act
(“CEQA”) in accordance with CEQA Guidelines §15378(b)(5), in that the transfer of the Property
does not meet CEQA’s definition of a “project” as it is an organizational or administrative activity
of governments that will not result in direct or indirect physical changes in the environment. The
proposed action is also exempt under §15312 for Surplus Government Property Sales as the
Property has no significant value for wildlife habitat or other environmental purpose and the use
of the parcel and adjacent property has not changed.

On April 5, 2024, as part of 2024-25 Annual Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule review
letter, DOF instructed the Successor Agency to transfer “Judges Parking Lot” property to the
City for immediate conveyance to Los Angeles County.

As a result, this item is necessary to transfer the property to the City for further transfer to the
County of Los Angeles for a governmental purpose to serve as a judges’ parking lot at the
adjacent courthouse.

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends the Successor Agency Board of Directors:
  a. adopt Resolution No. SA 24-02, A RESOLUTION OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO
  THE NORWALK REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY DECLARING CERTAIN PROPERTIES’
  GOVERNMENTAL PURPOSE AND REQUESTING THAT THE OVERSIGHT BOARD
  TO THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY APPROVE THE TRANSFER OF THE PROPERTY
  LOCATED AT 12710 NORWALK BOULEVARD TO THE CITY OF NORWALK;
  b. find that the Property will be used for a governmental purpose as a parking lot for judges’
  from the adjacent County courthouse pursuant to the Long Range Property Management
  Plan; and
  c. find that the Property is exempt surplus land pursuant to the exemptions under California
  Government Code §54221(f)(1)(C) and §54221(f)(1)(D); and that the transfer is not a
  “project” under CEQA Guidelines §15378(b)(5).

   Attachment No. 1

  RESOLUTION NO. SA 24-02

  A RESOLUTION OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE NORWALK
  REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY DECLARING CERTAIN PROPERTIES’
  GOVERNMENTAL PURPOSE AND REQUESTING THAT THE
  OVERSIGHT BOARD TO THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY APPROVE THE
  TRANSFER OF THE PROPERTY LOCATED AT 12710 NORWALK
  BOULEVARD TO THE CITY OF NORWALK

  WHEREAS, the former Norwalk Redevelopment Agency (“NRDA”) was dissolved
in accordance with California State Assembly Bill AB 1x26, as amended by Assembly Bill
1484 (“Dissolution Act”), and the California Supreme Court decision in California
Redevelopment Association, et al. v. Ana Matosantos, et al. 53 Cal.4th 231 (2011); and

  WHEREAS, the Dissolution Act also required the designation of a successor
agency to wind down the affairs of former redevelopment agencies and the appointment
of an oversight board of the successor agency to oversee, review and approve certain
actions of the successor agency in accordance with the requirements of the Dissolution
Act; and

  WHEREAS, upon dissolution of the NRDA, the real property assets and real
property interests of the NRDA were transferred to the Successor Agency to the Norwalk
Redevelopment Agency (“Successor Agency”); and

  WHEREAS, in 2013, the Successor Agency developed a Long-Range Property
Management Plan (“LRPMP”) governing the disposition and use of the former real
property interests and assets of the NRDA, and was approved by the prior oversight board
of the Successor Agency (“Oversight Board”) and submitted to the California Department
of Finance (“DOF”) for approval; and
  WHEREAS, the LRPMP included a designation for (“Parcel 8a”) located at 12710
Norwalk Boulevard (APN: 8047-006-922) for governmental purpose to be used as a future
parking lot for judges from the adjacent Superior Court building; and
  WHEREAS, in accordance with an (“Option Agreement”) referenced in the
LRPMP, the NRDA constructed a 25-space enclosed parking on Parcel 8a, with the
intention of exchanging the parcel for a nearby parking lot owned by the County of Los
Angeles (“County”), referred to as (“Parcel 8b”) upon completion; and
  WHEREAS, in 2014, the DOF mandated specific revisions to the LRPMP including
the deletion of the Parcel No. 8b from the LRPMP as this parcel had not yet been
separated from the larger parcel owned by the County; and
  WHEREAS, pursuant to California Health and Safety code Section 34179(q), in
2018, the oversight boards for successor agencies to former redevelopment agencies
were consolidated into five oversight board under the jurisdiction of Los Angeles County,
 and jurisdiction for the Successor Agency falls under the Los Angeles County Fourth
Supervisorial District Consolidated Oversight Board (“Oversight Board”); and

  WHEREAS, the Dissolution Act, per Health and Safety Code §34181(a), allows
the Oversight Board to direct the Successor Agency to transfer ownership of assets that
were constructed and used for a governmental purpose to the appropriate public
jurisdiction pursuant to existing agreements relating to the construction and use of the
asset; and
  WHEREAS, the “governmental purpose” examples listed in Health and Safety
Code §34181(a) include parking facilities and lots dedicated solely to public parking that
do not generate revenues in excess of reasonable maintenance costs of the properties;
and
  WHEREAS, Parcel 8a and the parking structure located thereupon, fall within the
parameters of a “governmental purpose” per Health and Safety Code §34181(a) and the
Oversight Board may direct the Successor Agency to transfer Parcel 8a to the appropriate
public jurisdiction; and
  WHEREAS, per Health and Safety Code §34181(f) the transfer of Parcel 8a shall
be approved by a resolution of the Oversight Board approving and/or directing the transfer
at a public meeting held with ten (10) days advanced notice to the public, and subject to
approval by the DOF; and:
  WHEREAS, the transfer of Parcel 8a is exempt from the AB 1486 (“Surplus Land
Act”) under California Government Code §54221(f)(1)(C) and §54221(f)(1)(D) in that
Parcel 8a is being transferred to another local agency’s use for the purpose of eventually
exchanging the parcel for another property necessary for the agency’s use; and
  WHEREAS, the proposed action is exempt from the requirements of the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) in accordance with CEQA Guidelines §15378(b)(5), in
that the transfer of Parcel 8a does not meet CEQA’s definition of a “project”, the action
constitutes organizational or administrative activities of governments that will not result in
direct or indirect physical changes in the environment. The proposed action is also
exempt under §15312 for Surplus Government Property Sales as the property has no
significant value for wildlife habitat or other environmental purpose and the use of the
parcel and adjacent property has not changed; and
  WHEREAS, in order to facilitate the transfer of Parcel 8a from the Successor
Agency to the City, the Successor Agency must request and the Oversight Board must
approve the transfer.
  NOW, THEREFORE, THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE NORWALK
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HEREBY DETERMINES, FINDS, AND RESOLVES AS
FOLLOWS:

Resolution No. 24-02  Page 2 of 6
   Section 1. The facts set forth in the Recitals, above, are true and correct and
incorporated herein as part of the findings of this resolution.

  Section 2. Based upon staff presentations, reports, discussions, public
comments, and other evidence presented, and subject to Oversight Board authorization
and appeal period by the DOF, the Successor Agency hereby finds and declares that
Parcel 8a, as further described in Exhibit A attached to this resolution, was constructed
an used for a governmental purpose as defined by Health & Safety Code § 34181, and
the Successor Agency may transfer Parcel 8a to the City of Norwalk (“City”).

  Section 3. Based upon staff presentations, reports, discussions, public
comments, and other evidence presented, the Successor Agency hereby finds and
declares that the City is the “appropriate public jurisdiction” to which the Parcel 8a should
be transferred, in order to effectuate the exchange of parking structures for governmental
use pursuant to the Option Agreement.

  Section 4. Based upon staff presentations, reports, discussions, public comments,
and other evidence presented, the Successor Agency further finds and declares that the
transfer of Parcel 8a to the City will further the purposes and objectives of the Successor
Agency, in that it will conserve staff time and financial resources associated with including
Parcel 8a in a Long Range Property Management Plan, and will conserve resources of
the former NRDA for the benefit of the taxing entities by reducing ongoing maintenance
costs of the Successor Agency.

  Section 5. The Successor Agency hereby directs staff to recommend and request
that the Oversight Board approve the transfer of Parcel 8a located at 12710 Norwalk
Boulevard from the Successor Agency to the City in accordance with Health & Safety
Code §34181(a).

  Section 6. Upon Oversight Board approval of the transfer of the Parcel 8a to the
City, the Successor Agency hereby authorizes and directs the Successor Agency’s
Executive Director or designee to execute all documents reasonably necessary to transfer
title to the City and to take any other action and execute ancillary documents reasonably
necessary to implement the intent of this Resolution.

  Section 7. The Successor Agency also hereby declares Parcel 8a to be “exempt
surplus land” under Government Code §54221(b)(1), and finds that the action falls under
the exemptions to the Surplus Land Act §54221(f)(1)(C) and §54221(f)(1)(D) for the
transfer or exchange of property necessary for the local agency’s use for the reason
stated herein.

  Section 8. If any section, subsection, paragraph, sentence, clause, phrase, or
portion thereof, of this Resolution is declared by a court of competent jurisdiction to be
unconstitutional or otherwise invalid, such decision shall not affect the validity of the
remaining portions of this Resolution. The Successor Agency declares that it would have
adopted this Resolution, and each section, subsection, paragraph, sentence, clause,

 phrase, or portion thereof, irrespective of the fact that any one or more sections,
subsections, paragraphs, sentences, clauses, phrases, or portions thereof, be declared
invalid or unconstitutional. To this end, the provisions of this Resolution are declared to
be severable.

  Section 9.  This Resolution shall become effective immediately upon its
approval.

  Section 10. The Successor Agency Secretary is hereby authorized to affix his or
her signature to this Resolution signifying its adoption by the Successor Agency.

  APPROVED AND ADOPTED on this 6th day of August 2024.
